hypothesis: Preserve raw-query and canonical-query retrieval hits as separate RRF evidence channels so cross-variant candidate corroboration affects ranking without changing reranker inputs or final selection.
why_now: Canonical alternates exist for 40/130 review rows, but current per-modality deduplication discards their second rank contribution. This is distinct from rejected alias expansion, candidate pruning, and selection changes.
expected_effect: Improve pre-rerank placement of corroborated candidates on canonical-alternate queries while preserving raw-only behavior.
success_signal: Cross-variant hits gain their independent normal RRF terms in focused tests, while raw-only and alternate-failure paths retain existing behavior; outer public/hidden guardrails remain non-regressive.
candidate_hypotheses: query_variant_evidence_fusion: retain raw and canonical ranks through RRF.
query_evidence_preservation: repair embedded quantity/clause-boundary truncation in canonical alternates.
catalog_scope_and_request_intent: conservatively expose uncertainty for affirmatively non-catalog service/consumable requests.
plan_summary: Created and strictly validated OpenSpec proposal, specification, design, and tasks for retrieval-fusion only at openspec/changes/v2-cycle-02-query-variant-evidence-fusion.
information_gain: Tests whether accepted canonicalization is bottlenecked by evidence collapse before RRF, rather than alternate queries being redundant or the primary issue being catalog scope.
